newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Senate votes for moratorium on human cloning.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Senate votes for moratorium on human cloning.

text.p: Spurred to action by the cloning of a sheep in Scotland, California's Senate voted on Thursday to impose a five-year moratorium on human cloning in the state.
The Senate approved the bill on a vote of 36-to-0, sending the measure to the state Assembly for review.
State Senator Patrick Johnston, who introduced the bill, said a moratorium was a rational response to the recent scientific discovery in Scotland, which may lead the way to human cloning.
Johnston, a Democrat who chairs the state Senate Select Committee on Genetics and Public Policy, said the moratorium would give the state time to evaluate the implications of cloning.
In February, Ian Wilmut and colleagues at the Roslin Institute in Edinburgh, Scotland announced they had cloned an adult sheep, the first time an adult animal had been cloned.
The announcement sparked a worldwide furore over whether this could eventually lead to cloning of humans.
In March, President Bill Clinton banned federally funded human cloning in the United States.
